summary: Slash commands in Claude Code are custom prompts that extend functionality by allowing users to create reusable commands with parameters. They enable workflow automation and consistent interactions.

sections.title: What are Slash Commands
sections.content: Slash commands are custom prompts stored as Markdown files that can be invoked using a forward slash. They act as reusable templates that can accept parameters and help standardize common workflows.
bestPractices: Keep slash commands focused on a single task
Use descriptive names that indicate the command's purpose

sections.title: Creating Slash Commands
sections.content: Slash commands are created by placing Markdown files in the ~/.claude/slash directory. The filename becomes the command name. Commands can include parameter placeholders using $1, $2, etc.

codeExamples.code:
# Review Pull Request

Please review this pull request: $1

Focus on:
- Code quality and best practices
- Potential bugs or issues
- Performance implications
- Security considerations
codeExamples.description: Example slash command template for PR reviews

codeExamples.code:
echo '# Explain Code

Please explain this code in detail:

```
$1
```' > ~/.claude/slash/explain.md
codeExamples.description: Creating a slash command via command line

warnings: Slash command files must have .md extension
Command names should not contain spaces or special characters
bestPractices: Include usage instructions in the command template
Test commands thoroughly before relying on them

sections.title: Built-in Slash Commands
sections.content: Claude Code includes several built-in slash commands for common tasks like /help, /clear, and /save. These provide quick access to frequently used functionality.
